chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, saying: Eesa ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, the Commander of the Faithful, that he said:
The master of this matter is from my progeny. It is he, about whom it will be said: He died or perished? No, but [he is alive] in whichever valley he has entered.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The master/leader of the matter (referring to the Imam of the Age)
key_terms.مَاتَ أَوْ هَلَكَ: He died or perished (common saying about the hidden Imam)
key_terms.وَادٍ سَلَكَ: Entered a valley (metaphor for a state of concealment or journey)

ai.seo_question: Who is the master of the matter from the progeny of Ali and how is his disappearance described?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the Shia doctrine of the Imam's occultation by affirming that the leader of the final deliverance is from the progeny of Ali ibn Abi Talib. It directly counters the doubt of those who claim he has died, asserting instead that he remains alive and concealed in a specific location ('in whichever valley he has entered'), a concept central to the theology of the Hidden Imam.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (18) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi from Eessa bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Umar bin Ali bin Abu Talib from his father from his grandfather that his father Amirul Mo’mineen Ali bin Abu Talib (as) had said:
“The master of this matter (deliverance) will be from my progeny. It is he, about whom it will be said: Has he died or perished? Or which valley has he followed?”
